SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate NEW PROGRAMS: COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: Creation of a Business Analytics and Intelligence Minor: See Appendix A The Business Analytics and Intelligence program is to provide students with the opportunity to better integrate data insights into their analyses and decision-making process. The program is also designed to strengthen knowledge from their primary major with advanced business analytics skills. Students will be prepared to bring insights from the large amounts of data to their functional areas such as marketing, finance, supply chain management, accounting among others. Students will specialize in one of the functional areas of business to gain additional skills that will prepare them for data-driven and analytics-based decision making. A minimum of six courses (18 credits) with an overall GPA of 2.0. A GPA of 2.0 (includes all attempts) is mandatory for the minor. Half of the credits for the minor (3 courses) must be completed at URI. All the courses for the minor must be taken at an AACSB accredited business school, at the URI Data Science program (CSC 201 or CSC 211) or through an approved study abroad program. 1

THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND Revised 8/2016 Notice of Change form Notice of Change for: Creation of a Business Analytics and Intelligence Minor Date: 10/16/20 A.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages).
Business Analytics and Intelligence (BAI) is the area of study that deals with skills, technologies, practices for efficient data management, continuous iterative exploration and investigation of business performance to gain insight and drive business planning.
There are an increasing number of BAI tools and methodologies newly introduced to the industry and academia every day.

These tools and methodologies provide field practitioners with statistical and operations analysis, the formation of predictive models, application of optimization techniques, and the communication of these results to customers, business partners, and college executives.
Business Analytics and Intelligence requires quantitative methods and evidence-based data for business modeling and decision making.
Business Analytics and Intelligence provide the industry with a great deal of benefits.
Data management solutions and analytical software continue to proliferate and provide better decision-making tools.
Businesses are increasingly relying on business analytics to gain a competitive advantage or just to keep up with the competition.
As such, students trained with BAI programs are highly-demanding future employees.
According to the U.S.
Bureau of Labor Statistics, Data scientist salaries in the United

States: $130,290 (2017), and Data scientist was ranked at #1 among 50 best jobs in America (Glassdoor.com).
Business analysts often specialize in a particular industry, such as medical science, telecommunications and energy.
Or, they may work in a specific area of business, like marketing, human resources or supply chain management.
In particular, those who are working for smaller firms may serve as general practitioners.
In all settings, the job of these professionals is to define a problem, collect and analyze data pertaining to it, evaluate company processes and procedures, and ultimately recommend and deploy strategies designed to solve the issue.
The Business Analytics and Intelligence program is to provide students with the opportunity to better integrate data insights into their analyses and decision-making process.
The program is also designed to strengthen knowledge from their primary major with advanced business analytics skills.
Students will be prepared to bring insights from the large amounts of data to their functional areas such as marketing, finance, supply chain management, accounting among others.

Students will specialize in one of the functional areas of business to gain additional skills that will prepare them for data-driven and analytics-based decision making.
Many of the courses of the program will be revised to include the important learning goals specific to Business Analytics and Intelligence.
Some courses listed in the COB curriculum will be tailored for BAI students.
The program will offer the courses of business statistics and mathematics, business application programming, data analytics software, e-Commerce, data management and visualization.
These courses were offered for the Management Information Systems (MIS) major in the college of business.
A minimum of six courses (18 credits) with an overall GPA of 2.0.
A GPA of 2.0 (includes all attempts) is mandatory for the minor.
Half of the credits for the minor (3 courses) must be completed at URI.
All the courses for the minor must be taken at an AACSB accredited business school, at the URI Data Science program (CSC 201 or CSC 211) or through an approved study abroad program.

Marine Affairs URI’s Department of Marine Affairs offers the following degrees: B.A., B.S., M.A., M.M.A. (Master of Marine Affairs), and Ph.D.
The B.A. and B.S. in marine affairs focus on coastal and ocean areas and examine environmental resources, human uses, and governance from a variety of perspectives.
Both degrees qualify for New England Regional Tuition.
Topics include conservation, ocean policy and law, climate adaptation and resilience, tourism and recreation, environmental justice, ocean energy resources, coastal and island communities, ports and shipping, fisheries and marine ecosystems, spatial planning and management.
A marine affairs major establishes a background for careers in the public or private sectors in a wide variety of marine-related fields.
Typical areas of employment include positions in government concerned with coastal zone, environmental, or fishery management, and marine transportation.
In the private sectors, students have secured positions in environmental consulting firms, marine insurance, public interest nongovernmental organizations, marinas, ports, and companies involved in shipping.

The major serves well as an educational background for continued study in law, especially environmental, fishery, coastal zone, admiralty, and ocean law.
Students have also entered graduate and professional programs in environmental management, public administration, community planning, marine affairs, and related fields.
Students in the Department of Marine Affairs who participate in the New England Regional Student Program must maintain a 2.80 G.P.A. and take at least one MAF course per year to retain their New England regional tuition status.
Failure to meet these objectives will result in suspension of the reduced tuition privilege.
Reinstatement may occur if the student meets these requirements for one year after the time of the suspension.
